title: Pop Foundations: The 60s Birth of Modern Music

walkthroughs.body_html:
Rock 'n' Roll emerged in the 1950s from blues, country and R&B. Elvis Presley became its biggest star; Chuck Berry shaped the guitar riffs.

Songs often use a 12-bar blues pattern, driving backbeat (snare on 2 and 4), and short 'hook' choruses you can sing instantly.

The Beatles (Lennon, McCartney, Harrison, Starr) released their first single in 1962. By 1967's Sgt. Pepper, they had transformed pop with studio innovation, varied structures and sitar/orchestra additions.

Listen for tight vocal harmonies, inventive chord changes (e.g. Strawberry Fields) and concept albums that treated pop as art.

The Motown label, founded 1959 by Berry Gordy, produced polished soul hits — Marvin Gaye, Stevie Wonder, The Supremes, The Temptations.

The 'Motown sound' features tight rhythm sections, prominent tambourine on the backbeat, brass riffs and slick call-and-response vocals.
